summary:
Space Is Closer Than It Seems is an interactive educational project that uses augmented reality (AR) to bring the stories of human-made objects left on the Moon and Mars closer to students and the public.

We selected four space artifacts representing different stages of planetary exploration: Luna 2, Surveyor 1, the Apollo 11 lunar laser retroreflector, and NASA’s Perseverance rover. For each artifact, our team created a short educational video explaining its mission, scientific purpose, and contribution to space exploration.

Using Artivive, we connect each video to a visual AR marker. When users scan the image with a smartphone, the story comes to life directly on the screen.

The project transforms complex scientific and historical information into an accessible and engaging experience. It shows that even spacecraft and instruments that have completed their missions can continue to inspire learning and help us understand the history of space exploration.

Our concept can be expanded with more artifacts, interactive maps of the Moon and Mars, and additional AR educational stories.
details:
Space Is Closer Than It Seems is an interactive educational project that combines NASA data, augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence (AI), and multimedia technologies to bring the stories of human-made objects left on the Moon and Mars closer to students and the wider public.

Our project focuses on four space artifacts: Luna 2, Surveyor 1, the Apollo 11 lunar laser retroreflector, and NASA’s Perseverance rover. We selected these objects because they represent important milestones in humanity’s exploration of the Moon and Mars.

The development process involved several technologies, each serving a specific purpose:

  • NASA – our primary source of scientific and historical information. We researched the history of space missions, the purpose of each object, its scientific contribution, and its significance for space exploration.
  • Artivive – used to create the augmented reality experience by connecting educational videos with corresponding images. When users scan an image with a smartphone, the video appears directly on the image, turning a static visual into an interactive AR object.
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI) – used as an assisting technology in the preparation and production of multimedia content.
  • ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech – used to generate voice narration for our educational videos.
  • AI Free Video (Image-to-Video) – used to transform selected static images into short video sequences, making the stories more dynamic and visually engaging.

For each artifact, our team researched reliable sources, developed an educational story, prepared the visual materials, and created a short video explaining the mission, its objectives, and its contribution to science.

The main advantage of our project is that it transforms complex scientific and historical information into an accessible, visual, and interactive learning experience. Instead of simply reading about space missions, users can scan an image and watch the story of a real space artifact come to life.

The project is creative because it combines authentic space exploration history with AR and AI-assisted technologies in an educational format. It also encourages a new perspective on objects left on other celestial bodies: even after their missions end, they remain important symbols of scientific progress and human curiosity.

We expect the project to increase students’ interest in astronomy, space exploration, science, and digital technologies. It can also be used in classrooms, educational exhibitions, science events, and interactive learning activities.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, the reliability of information sources, accessibility, ease of use, visual quality, and responsible AI use. AI tools supported the creative production process but did not replace the team's research or decision-making. The scientific facts were checked against NASA materials and other reliable sources, while the project concept, selection of artifacts, storylines, scripts, and AR design were developed by the team.

In the future, Space Is Closer Than It Seems can be expanded with more space artifacts, interactive maps of the Moon and Mars, additional AR stories, and educational materials.
